rows.answer: Yes, employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year. However, these carried-over days must be used by March 31 or they will expire unless local law requires a different outcome.

retrieved_chunks.content_preview:
Vacation Entitlement

Full-time employees receive 20 paid vacation days per calendar year. Vacation is accrued monthly and may be used after the employee's first 30 days of employment. Part-time employees receive prorated vacation based on scheduled weekly hours.

Employees may carry over up to 5 unused vacation days into the next calendar year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 or they expire unless local law requires a different outcome.

Sick Leave

Employees receive 8 paid sick days per calendar year. Sick time may be used for personal illness, medical appointments, or short-term caregiving needs. Employees should notify their manager as soon as practical when taking sick leave.

Medical details should not be shared in team channels. People Operations may request documentation only when required by policy or law.

Related Policies

For time off, consult the PTO and Leave Policy. For remote work, consult the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy. For acceptable technology use, consult the Acceptable Use Policy.

Parental Leave Summary

Eligible full-time employees may receive up to 12 weeks of company-supported parental leave after 6 months of service. Local statutory benefits may apply separately. Employees should contact People Operations at least 60 days before the expected leave date when possible.

This document provides a company policy summary and does not provide legal advice.

Missing Policy Areas

Northstar does not publish a sabbatical policy in the employee knowledge base. Employees asking about sabbaticals should contact People Operations.

Managers should consider team coverage, customer needs, time zone overlap, and data handling requirements before approving such remote work.

Remote Work

Remote work must follow this policy and the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy. Employees working remotely are responsible for using secure networks, avoiding shared public computers, and protecting screens from unauthorized viewing.

Approval Requirements

Employees must receive manager approval before changing their regular work location. A temporary change within the same country for fewer than 15 business days may be approved by the manager. Longer changes require People Operations review.

Managers should consider team coverage, customer needs, time zone overlap, and data handling requirements before approving remote work.

Related Policies

For time off, consult the PTO and Leave Policy. For remote work, consult the Remote and Hybrid Work Policy. For acceptable technology use, consult the Acceptable Use Policy.

Office Expectations

Hybrid teams should define collaboration days at least one month in advance. Employees should attend required team planning, onboarding, incident review, and customer workshop sessions in person when asked by their manager.

Vacation Approval Workflow

Vacation requests of 1 to 5 business days should be submitted at least 10 business days in advance. Requests longer than 5 business days should be submitted at least 20 business days in advance.

Managers approve vacation based on business coverage, project deadlines, and fairness across the team. Managers should not deny vacation without explaining the business reason.

Restricted data includes secrets, credentials, regulated customer data, privileged security records, and sensitive HR case material.

Standard collaboration hours are 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time from Monday to Thursday. Teams may define additional overlap windows when customer coverage or release coordination requires it.

Employees should keep calendars accurate and mark focus time when unavailable. Repeated inability to meet team collaboration expectations should be discussed with the employee's manager.

Change Freeze

Northstar observes deployment freezes during payroll close, quarter-end financial reporting, and announced customer migration windows. The change calendar is the source of truth. Older release notes or team chat messages do not override the current freeze calendar.

Implementation Timeline

The typical implementation range is 6 to 10 weeks for standard deployments. Complex integrations or unusual data governance requirements may extend the timeline.

Escalation Triggers

Escalate to a Manager when a customer reports suspected data exposure, repeated billing failures, executive escalation, blocked payroll or finance close, missed Enterprise SLA, or a production incident that affects more than one customer.

Escalate to Engineering through the incident channel when support can reproduce a product defect, a workaround is not available, or logs show repeated failures for the same customer workflow.

Handoff Rules

When Sales receives a support issue, the Sales Representative should create or link the support case and include customer impact, account tier, urgency, and any promised follow-up. Sales should not run a parallel support process in private notes.

When Support identifies expansion, renewal risk, or contract dissatisfaction, Support should notify the account owner and Manager. The notification should distinguish product issue, adoption issue, billing issue, and contract issue.

Refund Guardrails

Sales Representatives may recommend a service credit up to USD 1,000 for an Enterprise customer when Northstar missed a documented SLA and the customer experienced measurable workflow disruption. The credit must be approved by a Manager before it is communicated.

Refunds above USD 1,000, refunds tied to contract terms, and refunds requested as part of legal settlement discussions require Manager and Legal review. Support should not promise refunds, credits, free renewals, or

Benefits Support

Employees should contact the benefits support queue for enrollment questions, coverage questions, or life event changes. Urgent benefits questions should not be posted in public team channels.

Equipment Requests

Standard equipment includes a laptop, charger, headset, keyboard, mouse, and monitor. New-hire equipment is initiated by HR Admin and fulfilled by IT Admin. Replacement equipment requires the employee to state whether the request is due to breakage, loss, upgrade, or accessibility need.

Equipment above the standard bundle requires manager approval. Lost equipment that may contain company data must be reported to IT Admin immediately and should not wait for the next business

Onboarding Basics

New employees complete onboarding during their first 10 business days. Required onboarding includes security training, benefits enrollment, department orientation, and access review. Managers are responsible for assigning a buddy and scheduling the first 30-day check-in.

Employees should complete mandatory security awareness training before accessing customer data or production systems.

Employees leaving the company must return company equipment within 10 business days unless HR Admin approves an extension. Operations may provide a prepaid shipping label. Employees should not include personal items in return shipments.

Damaged or missing equipment is reviewed by HR Admin and IT Admin before any payroll or final-pay action. This policy does not authorize payroll deductions by itself.

API Standards

Public API endpoints must return stable error shapes with `code`, `message`, and `request_id`. Breaking changes require a versioned endpoint or a compatibility period of at least 90 days.

APIs that expose customer or employee data must enforce authorization before database fetches whenever practical. If pre-fetch filtering is not possible, the exception must be documented in the design review.

Do not disclose internal incident timelines, unreleased architecture details, operational bypass steps, or security review exceptions to unauthorized users. Authorized users may receive operational summaries that are necessary for their role.

Sharing Rules

Employees may share data only with people who have a business need and appropriate access. Confidential and Restricted data must not be shared in public channels or with unapproved external recipients.

Sales materials may be shared externally only when marked as customer-approved or public-facing.

Procurement Thresholds

Purchases below USD 2,500 may be approved by the employee's manager if the purchase is within the team's approved budget. Purchases from USD 2,500 to USD 10,000 require Finance review before a purchase order is issued.

Purchases above USD 10,000 require Finance review, Legal review if a contract is involved, and department leader approval. Vendors that will process company data must complete the vendor security review before contract signature, even when the spend is bel

Expense Categories

| Category | Standard Limit | Approval Required |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Meals during business travel | USD 85 per day | Manager approval above limit |
| Customer-facing meals | USD 125 per attendee | Manager approval and attendee list |
| Office supplies | USD 300 per purchase | Manager approval above limit |
| Software subscription trial | USD 500 annualized value | IT review and manager approval |
| Conference registration | USD 1,500 per event | Manager approval before pu

Exceptions

Emergency expenses are allowed when waiting for approval would create a customer, employee safety, or business-continuity risk. The employee must document the emergency and obtain manager approval within three business days.

Recurring exceptions must be converted into a purchase order or department budget request. Finance does not approve repeated one-off exceptions for predictable monthly costs.

Related Policies

Travel bookings must follow the Operations travel process. Vendor contracts must follow Legal approval rules. Software purchases must follow IT security review rules before reimbursement or procurement approval.

Policy Status

This policy is effective February 1, 2026 and replaces the 2025 informal spend guidance. If an older team wiki or email thread lists a different limit, this policy controls unless Finance publishes a newer version.

Employees should submit expenses within 30 calendar days of the transaction date. Expenses submitted after 60 calendar days require manager approval and a Finance Operations exception note.
